title: Failover: Choosing the Right Recovery
context: A major power outage hits the primary site. You must decide on the recovery strategy in three steps.

n1.text: Before failing over, which metric must you know first?

choices.text: The RPO and RTO of critical services
choices.why: Without quantified objectives, it is impossible to choose an appropriate site or strategy.
The vendor alone does not determine the strategy.
Useful for communication, not for choosing recovery.

n2.text: The payment service requires recovery in under 5 minutes and zero data loss. Which site?

choices.why: A cold site takes days and implies data loss.
Only a hot site offers near-zero RPO and failover in minutes.
A warm site requires restoration: RPO and RTO are too high.

n3.text: After power is restored, which step is often forgotten?

choices.why: Returning to the primary site and verifying consistency is essential.

choices.text: Permanently shutting down the backup site
choices.why: The backup site must remain available for the next recovery.
Backups are valuable, especially after an incident.

n4.outcome: You reasoned in terms of RTO/RPO, chose the right site, and planned for failback.

debrief: Hot site = minutes and near-zero loss; warm site = hours; cold site = days.
Failback and restoration testing are part of resilience.
